\begin{CRchronicle}{76}
On Frost 10 the district’s arithmetic changed at the Cross and could not be changed back. Berr Clay wiped his thumb twice, passed a finger over a figure, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} low into the two hundred, called the levy and denied it --- \emph{your house}, never \emph{I} --- and went off to High Kiln with Frost’s first true subtraction locked in his box, believing he had done a kindness. The bell went four, four and a gap and nobody crossed himself. Hessa Rale carried his slate up the road unread; the soft-cuffed clerk sat below the north bridge for a measure nobody called.

The reading knew nothing of what it read over. It went over the basket in the moot-post’s shade and left no figure in it, answered nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15. The dressed grain lay covered under wool on the cool stone, read over by a number that did not know what it cost, the space between figure and price unsigned. One gesture ran through the square at different scales: a thane’s finger over a figure, a runner’s hand to a slate, a clerk’s number entered before his eyes found the buyer, a widow carrying a basket at a half-pace. Each hand went to its object first.

The two mornings after were ordinary: no market, no Cross, no bell. Sella went to the fire before the basket, said \emph{The house will keep it}, gave neither gap of the row a figure, turned the dressed grain beneath the wool and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand. Ilva drew water at the well, her hand toward her sleeve, and answered only \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account.} Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, stopped the ear-sentence short of calling the loan; Jorra kept dusty forearms from clean and withheld his knowing. The frost lay white on the well lip and the plate of ice stood on its stone; the yard called both weather.

Through three days the hand rose an inch six times and came down six times on the river’s note --- a rhythm carried across a silence, the heard bell’s gap beside a breath, a letting-go left whole, two intakes bridged, a silence kept empty, the held interval beside the empty one --- each filed exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, not a reach, not a hearing, not a gift. At the close two hundred and eighty-one stood unspent and spoken by nobody; six months and one hundred and one days were told by nobody; the fire’s fifth was unpaid the same number of days, its payer unnamed. The file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap, the crust two inches off, and the river’s note went quiet.
\end{CRchronicle}
